setting.media_analysis.enabled.help: Makes AI video detection available to the parts of the platform that ask for it. It never analyses media on its own: each form or module decides where it is used.
Files larger than this are refused before anything is sent. Empty adds no limit beyond the analyzer's own.
setting.media_analysis.min_video_duratio: An analysis of a video or audio file shorter than this is refused. Uploading is never affected. Empty is no minimum.
setting.media_analysis.max_video_duratio: An analysis of a video or audio file longer than this is refused, and nothing is sent to the analyzer. Uploading is never affected. Empty adds no limit beyond the analyzer's own.
setting.media_analysis.duration_range_in: The shortest duration to analyse cannot be longer than the longest.
setting.media_analysis.daily_limit.help: The most analyses that may be requested in a day, across every use. Empty is no daily limit.
setting.media_analysis.timeout_seconds.h: How long one analysis may run before it is given up on.
setting.media_analysis.likely_synthetic_: A score at or above this (0 to 1) is classified likely synthetic. Advisory: the scores are always recorded, and each use may apply its own threshold. Empty derives no classification.
setting.media_analysis.likely_authentic_: When every score is at or below this (0 to 1), the media is classified likely authentic. Empty derives no such classification.

How long a deleted file is kept before the daily purge removes it for good.

setting.auth.captcha_enabled.help: Require a captcha check when somebody signs in. The active captcha provider decides how it is checked; with no provider configured, sign-in is refused rather than let through unchecked.
setting.auth.captcha_site_key.help: The public half of the captcha credentials. A browser has to be given it, so it is published to any client that asks; the secret half lives encrypted on the provider row and never leaves the server.
setting.auth.captcha_version.help: Which reCAPTCHA generation the site key belongs to: v2 shows a challenge, v3 scores silently. Set it to match the key, not to a preference.
setting.auth.otp_length.help: How many digits a delivered code has. Length is not where the security comes from — the lifetime and the attempt limit below are — so this is a legibility choice more than a strength one.
setting.auth.otp_lifetime_seconds.help: How long a delivered code stays valid, in seconds. The message tells the recipient this figure, so shortening it shortens what they are told.
setting.auth.otp_max_attempts.help: How many wrong answers a code survives before it is discarded. Guessing then costs a resend, and the resend costs the cooldown above.
setting.auth.otp_resend_cooldown_seconds: How long somebody must wait before asking for another code. A resend replaces the outstanding one, so two live codes never exist for one account.
setting.auth.password_min_length.help: The shortest password the platform accepts, applied everywhere one is set — signing up, an administrator creating an account, and the first-administrator command. Raising it does not invalidate passwords already stored.
setting.auth.registration_enabled.help: Whether a first sign-in through a social provider may create an account. Off, such a sign-in is refused rather than turned into an account. Accounts an administrator creates are not affected.
setting.auth.social_login_enabled.help: Offer signing in with an external provider to user accounts. Administrators never sign in this way. A provider is offered only once it is switched on and fully configured under integrations.
setting.auth.social_redirect_uris.help: The exact addresses a person is returned to after signing in with a provider, one entry per client, written as a JSON list. Register each one, exactly as written, as an authorized redirect URI on the provider's OAuth client — for Google, in Google Cloud Console. A sign-in naming any other address is refused, and with none listed social sign-in cannot start. In production each must use https and must not point at localhost.
setting.auth.password_reset_url.help: The page of your client application where a person chooses a new password. A reset email links to it with the token and the address added. Unset, account recovery sends nothing, and in production social registration stays closed until it is set. In production it must use https and must not point at localhost.
social_login.setup.issue.no_redirect_uri: No return address is configured, so no social sign-in can start.
social_login.setup.issue.unusable_redire: At least one return address cannot be used in this environment and is ignored.
social_login.setup.issue.password_reset_: No password reset page is configured, so an account created through a provider could not recover access.
The password reset page cannot be used in this environment, so no reset link is sent.
social_login.setup.issue.no_effective_pr: No provider is switched on with both its client id and its client secret.
api.error.auth.social_provider_unavailab: That sign-in provider is not available.
api.error.auth.social_invalid_redirect_u: That return address is not allowed for social sign-in.
api.error.auth.social_state_invalid: This sign-in could not be completed. Start again.
api.error.auth.social_provider_error: The sign-in provider could not confirm who you are. Try again.
api.error.auth.social_sign_in_refused: Signing in this way is not possible for this account.
api.error.auth.social_identity_not_linke: An account already uses this address. Sign in to it another way, then link this provider from your account.
api.error.auth.social_registration_close: New accounts cannot be created at the moment.
api.error.auth.password_reset_invalid: This password reset link is not valid or has expired. Request a new one.
api.error.user.promotion_refused_social_: This account cannot become an administrator while a social sign-in is linked to it. The account holder has to unlink every social sign-in first.
api.error.user.social_identity_administr: Social sign-in cannot be linked to an administrator account.
api.error.user.social_identity_identity_: This sign-in already belongs to another account.
api.error.user.social_identity_provider_: This account already has a sign-in linked from this provider.
api.error.user.social_identity_last_sign: This is the only way to sign in to the account. Set a password or link another provider before removing it.
api.error.user.social_identity_not_linke: That social sign-in is not linked to this account.
setting.auth.session_lifetime.help: How many minutes a signed-in session stays valid without activity. Shortening it does not end sessions already open; it applies from the next sign-in.
setting.branding.favicon.help: The small icon a browser shows in a tab and a bookmark. Stored as media like every other branding asset, so it goes through the same upload, scanning and delivery path.
setting.branding.logo_dark.help: The Arabic logo, for use on a dark background.
setting.branding.logo_dark_en.help: The English logo, for use on a dark background.
setting.branding.logo_light.help: The Arabic logo, for use on a light background. Four logos exist because a wordmark reads differently in each language and inverts differently on each background.
setting.branding.logo_light_en.help: The English logo, for use on a light background.
setting.branding.max_image_dimension.hel: The largest edge, in pixels, an uploaded image may have. Not enforced yet: measuring an image needs the processing pipeline, which this deployment has no image extension to run.
setting.branding.max_upload_kilobytes.he: The largest file the media endpoint accepts, in kilobytes. The web server carries a ceiling of its own, so this cannot raise the limit above what the server will pass.
setting.branding.og_image.help: The image a link to this platform shows when it is shared. Used as the default where nothing more specific has been set.
setting.branding.watermark_enabled.help: Whether derived image sizes carry the watermark below. Not applied yet: watermarking is a step in deriving an image, and no image processor runs in this deployment.
setting.branding.watermark_image.help: The image laid over derived sizes. Never over the original, which stays the archival copy — a watermark burned into it could not be removed later.
setting.branding.watermark_margin_percen: How far the watermark sits from the edge, as a percentage of the image.
setting.branding.watermark_opacity.help: How solid the watermark is, as a percentage. Lower is fainter.
setting.branding.watermark_position.help: Which corner, or the centre, the watermark sits in.
setting.branding.watermark_width_percent: How wide the watermark is drawn, as a percentage of the image it sits on, so it scales with the derivative rather than being fixed in pixels.
setting.general.admin_url.help: Where this console is served from. Recorded so a link back to it can be written into a message that is read somewhere else.
setting.general.comments_enabled.help: Whether the application built on this platform should accept comments. Published for that application to read; this foundation has no comments of its own.
setting.general.contact_job_title.help: The role shown beside the contact name, per language.
setting.general.contact_person.help: Who a visitor is told to ask for, per language.
setting.general.contact_phones.help: The numbers a visitor may call, as a list of up to ten. Numbers shown publicly rather than the ones the platform sends messages to.
setting.general.cookie_message.help: What the cookie notice says, per language. The wording only — whether a notice is shown at all is the decision of the front end.
setting.general.footer_copyright.help: The copyright sentence at the foot of a public page, per language.
setting.general.footer_text.help: What the foot of a public page says, per language.
setting.general.frontend_url.help: Where the visitor-facing application lives, when it is served separately from this API.
setting.general.location_latitude.help: Where this organisation is, for a map. Published with the longitude beside it.
setting.general.location_longitude.help: Where this organisation is, for a map. Published with the latitude beside it.
setting.general.maintenance_admin_bypass: Leave this on so the platform can be repaired through its own interface. With it off nobody reaches the API at all, including you, and maintenance can then only be switched off from the console or the database.
setting.general.maintenance_message.help: What a caller reads while the platform is closed. Written per language; a language with no message falls back to the platform default.
setting.general.maintenance_mode.help: While this is on the API answers every request with 503 and the message below. Administrators keep working if the bypass beneath is on.
setting.general.official_email.help: The address a visitor is told to write to. Not the address the platform sends from — that is the mail group.
setting.general.site_description.help: A sentence describing this platform, per language. Read where a short description is shown rather than a name.
setting.general.site_name.help: What this platform calls itself. Written per language, and read by anything that displays a name — a page title, an email signature, a share card.
setting.general.site_url.help: The address the public site is served from. Used where a full link has to be written rather than a relative path — an email, a share card, a canonical URL.
setting.localization.date_format.help: How a date is written where the platform publishes one for a client to render.
setting.localization.timezone.help: The zone the platform reasons in when a date has to be shown without one. Stored moments are always absolute; this decides how they read.
setting.mail.enabled.help: Whether the platform sends mail at all. With it off, a notification that would have been emailed is simply not sent by that channel.
setting.mail.encryption.help: How the connection to the mail server is protected. `none` sends credentials in the clear and is meant for a local server that never leaves the machine.
setting.mail.from_address.help: The address the platform sends from. A recipient replying to a message goes here unless the reply-to below is set.
setting.mail.from_name.help: The name shown beside the sending address, per language, so a recipient reads it in their own.
setting.mail.host.help: The mail server to connect to.
setting.mail.password.help: The credential for that account. Stored encrypted and never readable back — the console can say whether one is set and nothing more.
setting.mail.port.help: The port on that server. It has to agree with the encryption below — 587 for TLS, 465 for SSL, 25 for neither.
setting.mail.reply_to.help: Where replies should go, when that is not the sending address.
setting.mail.test_recipient.help: Where the test message goes. Only the test uses it; no notification is ever sent here.
setting.mail.transport.help: How mail leaves: an SMTP server, the application log, or an in-memory array. The last two exist for a deployment that must not send anything.
setting.mail.username.help: The account used to authenticate against the mail server.
How many days of the administrative trail stay in the active store. It decides which records an archival operation may take and never causes one to run: nothing removes an audit record on a schedule.
setting.operations.provider_retry_attemp: How many more times to try the same vendor when a connection to it could not be opened at all — its address did not resolve or it refused the connection. Nothing is retried once the vendor may have received the request: a timeout or an error answer goes to the next provider instead, so a message is never sent twice by a retry.
setting.operations.provider_timeout_seco: How long to wait on an external vendor before treating the attempt as failed. A failed attempt falls through to the next provider in the chain rather than raising.
setting.rate_limit.authenticated_ip_mult: How much of the per-caller limit an address may consume in total. It exists so that an office behind one address is not throttled as though it were one person.
setting.rate_limit.public_read_per_minut: How many times an unauthenticated caller may read, per minute, from one address. The same number bounds requests refused because their credentials were missing, expired or invalid: past it, those callers are told to wait rather than refused again.
setting.rate_limit.read_per_minute.help: How many times a signed-in caller may read, per minute.
setting.rate_limit.upload_per_hour.help: How many files one caller may upload in an hour.
setting.rate_limit.write_per_minute.help: How many times a signed-in caller may write, per minute. Lower than reads because a write costs more and is rarely issued in bursts.
setting.security.api_secret_key.help: A shared credential for a caller that is not a person. Stored encrypted and never readable back.
setting.security.decay_minutes.help: How many minutes a lockout lasts, and the window the attempts above are counted over.
setting.security.max_login_attempts.help: How many failed sign-ins are allowed before the account is locked out for the window below.
settings.rollback.skipped.dependency_uns: Restoring it would enable something whose prerequisite is no longer set.
settings.rollback.skipped.invalid_today: The stored value no longer satisfies this setting’s current rules.
settings.rollback.skipped.not_editable: This setting cannot be changed through the admin API.

settings.secret.verification.verified: Confirmed with the service before it was stored.

setting.ai.max_output_tokens.help: The ceiling on what a generation may return, in tokens. Without one, a model that misreads the instruction returns an essay and the operator pays for every token of it.
setting.ai.timeout_seconds.help: How long to wait for a generation. Separate from the vendor timeout, because a generation takes seconds by construction and that ceiling would fail requests that were working.
